title: How would you test AI dialogue inside a hybrid action-bar encounter? — V.E.T.O.R WIP
author: Sufficient-Cause2216
selftext:
I’m building V.E.T.O.R — A Ruptura, a Windows 2D platform adventure currently in development, and I’m testing a specific design question: can an enemy encounter feel more reactive when the player can talk to the NPC or enemy instead of only receiving fixed battle lines?

The Titan Theron encounter uses one action bar in two modes. In turn mode the character stays in place while the bar fills. In semi-turn mode the character can move freely, but attacking and defending still consume that same bar. The aim is to keep the timing readable while allowing dialogue to change the tone or direction of an encounter.

AI is part of both the production workflow and the game feature: Codex assists with programming and image work; Google Veo is used for promotional video scenes; and the project includes personality-driven AI conversations for NPCs and enemies. I’m responsible for the design decisions and integration, and there is no public demo or sale yet.

This is the Titan Theron development video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nOETh7lBx8M
Project site: https://vetorlogico.com/

I’d appreciate feedback from other AI game developers: what would you test first to make sure dialogue during combat adds meaningful choice rather than distracting from the action bar?
